title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
hook: Search agents forget what they've already tried and loop on failed queries, burning their budget. SearchOS gives them a shared, persistent memory of what's been searched, found, and failed.
key_points: As a search agent's interaction history grows, it struggles to track progress and can get stuck repeating failed search attempts.
SearchOS turns fragile, implicit progress into explicit shared state: a Frontier Task list, an Evidence Graph, a Coverage Map, and a Failure Memory.
It frames open-domain search as filling in a structured schema — discovering entities, populating linked attributes, and grounding every value in cited evidence.
A pipeline-parallel scheduler overlaps sub-agents and refills freed capacity with tasks targeting unresolved coverage gaps, instead of idling or repeating.
A middleware harness intercepts model/tool calls to log grounded evidence and react to stalls, plus a reusable skill system to avoid repeating failed search patterns.
Leads all evaluated single- and multi-agent baselines on the WideSearch and GISA benchmarks.
content_html:
Give a search agent a hard, multi-step question and it often does something frustrating: it keeps re-running searches it already tried, because nothing in its transcript tells it "this didn't work, stop." Yuyao Zhang, Zhicheng Dou, and collaborators (including Ji-Rong Wen) call this out as a core failure of current single- and multi-agent search systems, and build SearchOS to fix it.

The fix is to stop treating search progress as something implicit in a growing conversation history, and make it explicit, shared state instead: a running list of open sub-tasks, a graph of gathered evidence, a map of what's covered versus still missing, and a memory of what's already failed. On top of that shared state, SearchOS runs sub-agents in a pipeline-parallel way, continuously refilling idle capacity with work aimed at the gaps that remain — plus a middleware layer that intercepts every model/tool call to log evidence and catch stalls, and a reusable skill library so agents don't repeat the same failed search pattern across runs. On the WideSearch and GISA benchmarks, the authors report SearchOS leading all evaluated baselines.
extra_html: The framing worth remembering: SearchOS treats open-domain search as filling in a structured schema (entities, linked attributes, grounded citations) rather than free-form retrieval, which is what makes "coverage" and "what's still missing" a well-defined, trackable thing rather than a vibe. Full paper linked via the source.

flashcards.prompt: What core failure mode does SearchOS target in multi-agent search systems?
flashcards.back_html: Agents losing track of task progress as history grows, then getting stuck in repetitive loops on failed searches — wasting search budget and hurting output quality.

flashcards.prompt: How does SearchOS's Search-Oriented Context Management (SOCM) fix repetitive search loops?

choices.text: It externalizes progress into explicit shared state — a Frontier Task, Evidence Graph, Coverage Map, and Failure Memory
It simply increases each agent's context window size
It replaces all agents with a single larger model
It retries every failed query with a different random seed

flashcards.explanation_html: Instead of leaving progress implicit in a growing transcript, SOCM makes it explicit and persistent — so agents can see what's already been tried and target unresolved gaps instead of repeating failures.

flashcards.prompt: How does SearchOS frame the task of open-domain information seeking?
flashcards.back_html: As relational schema completion with grounded citations — discovering entities, filling in attributes across linked tables, and anchoring each value to source evidence.
